name: Littelfuse, Inc.
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow: the largest specialist in circuit protection with design-in and safety-certification switching costs and a broad portfolio, but components face Eaton/TE/Bourns/Bel/Mersen and low-cost Asian rivals, no network effects, and measured ROIC fell from 15.9% (2022) to 10.2% (2023), 4.1% (2024) and 1.1% (2025) on semiconductor impairments — a franchise that has not held returns well above the cost of capital through this cycle.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 5.0x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (6.2%) vs bull-case tier C (10.6%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Solid circuit-protection franchise, moat 5/10 — does not clear 15% at $380.89 on TTM OE (weighted IRR 8.71%, weighted IV@15% $177.94); it clears 15% only below $177.94 despite the strong 2026 recovery.
moat_for: Largest independent fuse / circuit-protection specialist; leading share in automotive fuses and PPTC resettable devices
Design-in switching costs: components are qualified into OEM designs and safety-certified, so sockets are sticky for a product generation
Broad portfolio across protection, power semiconductors, sensors and control (Basler, Dortmund fab) enabling cross-sell into data-center, grid and EV demand
Gross margin held 35.9-40.1% over the last five fiscal years despite the downturn
Conservative balance sheet: net debt $239.2M, 0.68x normalized OE, supports M&A and the dividend
moat_against: ROIC proxy collapsed from 15.9% in 2022 to 1.1% in 2025 (impairment-depressed, but ex-charge returns also fell) — no proof of durable excess returns through a cycle
$301.2M goodwill impairment in Electronics-Semiconductors (Q4 2025) after $93.5M of impairments in 2024: past semiconductor M&A destroyed value; Allen, TX fab closure announced for 2027
Components are contestable: Eaton, TE Connectivity, Bourns, Bel Fuse, Mersen and low-cost Chinese makers compete on price in standard parts
Cyclical end markets — autos, consumer electronics, HVAC, commercial vehicles — with a 2023-24 revenue decline still in the 3-yr CAGR (-1.73%)
Growth is partly bought: Basler ($350.3M, Dec 2025) and the Dortmund fab supplied much of recent inorganic growth
